claim: The interval between a tree's first commit and its first CI configuration shortened with each later tree, from thirteen days in logos to one day in anoieu and eudaimonia and zero in koine.
falsified_by: a CI configuration in logos before 2026-03-16 living under one of this run's excluded paths (deps/, checkers/, .lake/) or under a filename the apparatus detector does not recognise, which would make the thirteen-day gap an artifact of the detector rather than of the tree
scope: Covers only the presence and date of CI, test and manifest files. It says nothing about whether any of those jobs ran, passed, or checked anything, and nothing about ethos, which is not in the corpus.

claim: Ending a line of work is carried out in the trees and not only asserted in documents: two logos prefixes stopped after substantial commit counts and the child project the record says was folded into its parent shows as files moving.
falsified_by: a later pin of the same sources in which the CpcMicro or examples prefixes resume commits, or in which the anoieu_fuzz files move back out of tools, which would make logos-death-0013, logos-death-0014 and anoieu-transplant-0002 pauses rather than endings
scope: Three endings in two of five sources, all within one run's window. It does not cover whether the ending was the right call, and the fold-back happened one day after the child project started, which is too short a life to generalise from.

claim: The declared record includes entries that record the subject's own checks failing or being vacuous, rather than only completed items.
falsified_by: reading those five lines in place at the paths and line numbers given in claims.jsonl and finding they are template or aspirational text rather than records of a specific check that was found wrong
scope: Five claim lines out of 105, all from eudaimonia, dokimasia and koine, all written within four days. Nothing here shows the practice held over time, and logos, which is most of the history, contributes no claims at all.

claim: The tree holding four fifths of the ecosystem's commits contributes none of its declared record, so the documentation practice this corpus can see is three days old and applies only to the newest trees.
falsified_by: a declared record inside logos that the stage-3 extractor did not pick up — release notes, a TODO file, a dated discussion file — found by checking the extractor against the paths it did read in the other four sources (TODO.md, docs/discussion.md, docs/policy.md)
scope: This is a statement about what the extractor found in the five pinned trees. It cannot distinguish a tree that recorded nothing from a tree whose record is in a form or a place stage 3 does not read, and it says nothing about issue trackers or discussion threads, which are out of the corpus for every source.

claim: Governance documents were added and rewritten at a volume and rate that outran the trees they govern: a reporting policy revised six times on the day it was added and by 1,245 lines the next, a vision revised by 740 lines on its first day, a roles inventory by 485 on its first day, over trees between zero and three days old.
falsified_by: a run pinned some months later in which those same files show few or no further revisions, which would make 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-01 the drafting of a document that then held rather than churn
scope: Line counts of changes to five files in one source over three days. Churn is not quality: this does not show the documents were wrong, only that they were not yet stable, and the governance detector's threshold (governance_lines 40) means small revisions to the same files are absent from the count.

claim: The stage that joins the tree against the record produced a full classification of every event and claim while its matcher was disabled for four of five sources, and its four surviving matches join a claim to an event whose path repeats a word in the claim's text.
falsified_by: re-running stage 4 with delta_lag_days set small against the three-day source spans and finding the matched set substantially unchanged, which would show the six pairs are semantic matches rather than name collisions; the matcher source in bin/epikrisis is the second place to look
scope: About this run's delta stage and this tool, which is itself inside the subject under eudaimonia's tools prefix. It is not a claim about the detectors in stage 2, whose output the calibration result scored separately, and not a claim that the subject's record and trees actually disagree.
